answer: Trusted-execution attestation minting resists sybils: minting requires a hardware-backed remote attestation proving the work ran in a genuine secure enclave bound to distinct physical hardware, so one machine cannot cheaply mint many identities. A raven-fleet of fakes needs distinct attestable hardware per identity; an island of one enclave yields one binding. The pigment of each attestation is tied to real silicon, so a farm scaling to thousands needs thousands of attestable devices — a physical-hardware cost that cannot be collapsed onto one machine spinning many virtual identities.
